subject: Hosted API pilot — ops clarifications & rate/endpoint notes
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@finauto.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@finauto.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T16:10:00Z
Subject: Hosted API pilot — ops clarifications & rate/endpoint notes

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the Hosted API pilot so your engineering and infra teams can decide whether hosted will meet requirements or if Dedicated/Private is needed.

Recap (short):
- Use case: low-latency customer support summarization + contextual routing to knowledge base (live traffic initially in beta).
- Primary concerns you raised: sustained throughput during peak ingestion window, data residency for audit logs, and ability to test realistic rate profiles without impacting production.

Hosted quickstart proposal (what we can provision immediately):
- Sandbox endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/sandbox/finauto (read-only pilot workspace).
- Default soft rate limits for pilot: 40 requests/min per API key with 8 concurrent requests; burst window up to 120 requests/min for short testing periods. Token-level guidance: plan ~3–6k tokens/session for summarization flows.
- Endpoint mapping: we recommend separate endpoints for chat (chat-completions) and batch summarization to isolate throttling and metrics.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache can be enabled at route-level to reduce token spend for repeated prompts (we can enable a 10-minute TTL for the KB calls during the pilot).

Security / compliance notes:
- Hosted retains audit logs for 90 days by default; we can export logs to your S3 within the pilot period for review.
- We will share the security checklist and SOC summary (attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) Engineering sync (30–45m) to validate rate/profile numbers and confirm token budgets — Chloe to lead ops details.
2) Provide pilot workspace + keys (Marissa to coordinate account setup).
3) Run a two-week pilot with monitoring dashboard and a point-of-contact escalation plan.

If your team is comfortable with the default pilot limits above we can provision the sandbox today. Otherwise tell us expected RPS / sustained requests and we will map a Dedicated or Private sizing recommendation.

Action: Can you share the realistic peak requests/min you expect during a load spike (not average)? If you want, I can also sketch a Dedicated capacity estimate after the sync.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: finauto_pilot_scope.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: John Lee <john.lee@finauto.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@finauto.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T20:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot — ops clarifications & rate/endpoint notes

Thanks Alex — useful summary. A couple quick follow-ups from our infra/eng lead: 

1) The 40 reqs/min soft limit sounds low for our spike scenarios. On peak days we could hit 600–900 requests/min for the summarization flow for a 15–30m window. Is that within the sandbox burst behavior or do we need a Dedicated slice to test that?

2) Data residency: we need to confirm where the audit logs live and whether we can route them to our EU S3. If logs can only be retained for 90 days hosted-side, we'll need an export option to our bucket.

3) Endpoint mapping — can you confirm the chat vs batch endpoints you recommend and whether they will be rate-isolated? We want to ensure background batch jobs do not contend with user-facing chat traffic.

We reviewed the attached checklist and will share it with security, but wanted concrete answers on point 1–3 before scheduling the ops sync.

Best,
John
Head of Platform, FinAuto

On 2026-12-18 16:10, Alex Martinez wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the Hosted API pilot so your engineering and infra teams can decide whether hosted will meet requirements or if Dedicated/Private is needed.

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@finauto.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@finauto.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot — ops clarifications & rate/endpoint notes

John — thanks, great questions. Answers inline below and proposed schedule at the end.

1) Burst and peak handling:
- Sandbox default is conservative (40 reqs/min per key) to protect noisy testers. However, we can configure a pilot slice for FinAuto that raises soft limits to 1,200 requests/min with expected sustained ceilings of ~600 requests/min per slice depending on concurrency and average token length.
- For your 600–900 reqs/min 15–30m spikes, we recommend an initial hosted slice: 1,500 reqs/min soft, with a monitored burst to 2,500 reqs/min for short windows. That lets you test real traffic without committing to Dedicated immediately. If spikes are sustained beyond a day, Dedicated sizing is recommended.

2) Audit logs & residency:
- We can export audit logs continuously to your S3 (EU region) via an export connector — retention in your bucket is under your control. Hosted default retention remains 90 days, but export is recommended for compliance. We'll send the export setup doc after the sync.

3) Endpoint isolation:
- Yes, we recommend separate routes: /v1/hosted/finauto/chat for interactive chat; /v1/hosted/finauto/batch for background summarization. Each route will have independent rate caps and metrics. Background batch can be throttled independently to avoid contention.

Proposed next steps (pick one):
A) Ops sync (30m) this week: Chloe to run through traffic profile, token budgets, and export config.
B) Provision pilot slice (we'll set up the elevated limits above for 2 weeks + dashboard).

If you confirm A, Chloe is available Thursday 12/21 10:00–11:00 PT or Friday 12/22 08:00–11:00 PT. Which slot works?

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
